collapses anything larger into a single 'replace' opcode. A 2000-char paragraph vs. a 2000-char

there is no warning logged — the user has no idea why granular diffs disappeared. Consider emitting
a stderr warning, raising the cap, or switching to a linear-space Myers/Hirschberg algorithm for
long paragraphs.

[bug · high] --focus-ring uses color-mix(), which is Baseline 2023 (Chromium 111+/Safari
16.2+/Firefox 113+). On older WebView2 / Electron runtimes (or any user agent that doesn't recognize
color-mix) the *entire* `0 0 0 3px color-mix(...)` declaration becomes invalid, so box-shadow
computes to its initial `none` value — meaning .nm-btn, .nm-icon-btn and .nm-input lose their focus
ring entirely with no visual fallback. Because this token is also referenced from `:focus-visible`
rules on three critical interactive components, the failure is silent but a11y-breaking. Wrap the
color-mix declaration in @supports and provide a static rgba() fallback that uses the same
alpha-blended brand color, so the focus ring remains visible on legacy runtimes.

[performance · medium] The universal `*` selector applies `scrollbar-width: thin` and
`scrollbar-color` to every element in the document, including thousands of non-scrollable nodes
(text spans, icon children, inline elements). These properties are inexpensive per-element but force
style invalidation across the entire DOM on theme changes (because `scrollbar-color` references
`var(--t6)` which is recomputed in light/dark switches). Scope to known scroll containers (html,
body, `[data-scrollable]`, `.overflow-…`, or a small allow-list of class names) to keep invalidation
cost bounded.

[bug · medium] Dark mode is gated entirely on the `.dark` class which must be applied by JS. If the
bootstrap script fails to read the system preference, races against first paint, or is delayed

doesn't use `prefers-color-scheme` to gate the variables. Add a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)
{ :root:not(.light) { /* dark vars */ } }` block mirroring the `.dark` declarations so the initial
render matches the OS theme before JS settles, and so a JS failure still respects user intent.

[bug · medium] The self-documented rule `display: none` on `li br` swallows any `<br>` produced by
remark-breaks inside list items. While the comment justifies this for the inter-item spacing case,
it also hides legitimate intra-item line breaks the model emits for multi-line list content (e.g.
wrapped continuations, code-like spans, address blocks). This is a correctness regression: users
will see unrelated continuation text collapsed into a single line. Two safer fixes: (a) gate list
spacing on CSS `margin` between `li`s instead of a trailing `<br>`, or (b) hide only `<br>` that is
the last child of an `<li>` / directly follows `</li>`, leaving intra-item breaks intact.

and RFC 7235 §2.1 specify the auth-scheme token as case-insensitive; sending `bearer ` or `BEARER `

can leak via timing of `h.field.equiv(...)` resolution. Build the expected header value once with a
case-insensitive scheme (`format!("bearer {token}").into_bytes()` + `eq_ignore_ascii_case`) and
reject requests with more than one `Authorization` header.

`should_autostart` trusts them at the next launch — silent failure means a write may report success
to the API server while the disk flag never appears (next launch won't auto-start), or a stop may
report success while the flag remains (next launch auto-starts unexpectedly, possibly with a stale
token path). At minimum log the error; ideally return `Result<(), String>` and let the caller decide
whether to surface the inconsistency.

without the same atomic tmp+rename + fsync pattern used for the token. A crash, ENOSPC mid-write, or
an interrupted `write_enabled_flag` can leave a 0-byte or partial file that still passes the
existence check, so on next launch the app will try to bind the API server even though the user had
never explicitly enabled it. Validate the contents (e.g. `fs::read` and check it equals `b"1"`)
and/or have `write_enabled_flag` use the same tmp+rename pattern as `write_token_file` so partial
writes are impossible.

```rust
writeln!(f, ...)?;
// suggested: serialize only the append, rotate opportunistically
let _g = LOG_WRITE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| { ... });
if needs_rotate { crate::db::rotate_log_if_large(p, ...); }

```

and serializes the task, even when the EventHub has zero SSE subscribers. This fires on every write
hot path. Add a fast path on `EventHub::broadcast` that skips the send when there are no registered

─── src-tauri/src/api.rs:62-64 ───
[bug · high] Batch upsert is not atomic in MemStore: conflict check and apply are interleaved
per-task inside the for-loop. If the batch is `[A, B, C]` and only `C` carries `expected_updated_at`
(or only `C` conflicts), `A` and `B` are already written into `g` before the conflict error is
returned, so the caller sees a 409 while the store has silently applied a partial batch. The trait
takes `Vec<db::Task>` which strongly implies batch-level atomicity (and the surrounding 409/conflict
machinery is meant to guard exactly this), so MemStore should first compute all conflict decisions,
then apply the whole batch only if every task passes — or the contract should be documented as
"per-task partial apply allowed" and the production path must be verified to behave the same way.

─── src-tauri/src/api_server.rs:115-118 ───
[bug · high] last_id() is a lock-free SeqCst load while broadcast's fail-closed path mutates next_id
non-atomically from a reader's perspective. Race: thread A holds clients lock, fetch_add→5,
atomic_write fails, fetch_sub→4; a concurrent last_id() reader observes the transient 5, connects
with since=5, replay(5)=empty so writer sets last_sent=5. Thread B then succeeds with id=5 (because
A's fetch_sub restored the slot), pushes (5, msg) to history and live clients. The new writer
receives live event id=5 and drops it via `id <= last_sent`, silently losing the event. The "SeqCst
与 last_id() 的锁外读保持一致" comment is misleading — SeqCst preserves total order but not the invariant
"last_id = max actually-broadcast id" during the transient decrement window. Either keep next_id
monotonic on fail-closed (skip fetch_sub; persist next attempt), or record the gap separately so
last_id() returns the last *persisted+committed* id rather than the raw counter.



─── src-tauri/src/api_server.rs:120-126 ───
[performance · medium] The single `clients` lock guard spans fetch_add, db::atomic_write (disk I/O),
history.lock() (nested mutex acquisition), and an N-way try_send loop. A stalled disk, full history
mutex, or any sync_channel with a stalled writer blocks every broadcast — and `clients → history`
lock order is documented only as a "no other site" invariant, which is fragile for future
maintenance. Consider moving atomic_write outside the critical section (serialize id assignment into
a small bounded queue drained by a single persist task) or using a parking_lot Mutex with explicit
short critical sections, and document the lock-order contract in the type or with a debug_assert.



─── src-tauri/src/api_server.rs:136-139 ───
[bug · medium] `e.into_inner()` on a poisoned clients mutex silently recovers and continues; if the
panicking thread died mid-iteration in the try_send loop the Vec may be partially modified (e.g.,
indexes already advanced past a removed element, or a half-pushed entry). The history lock is even
more permissive — `if let Ok(...)` and replay's `Err(_) => Vec::new()` discard the poison error
entirely, so reconnecting clients get empty replay after a panic and lose events silently. Either
propagate the poison via `expect("history lock poisoned — refusing to drop events")` / return a
typed error so the caller / audit log records it, or rebuild the affected structure from the source
of truth rather than continuing on potentially torn state.



─── src-tauri/src/api_server.rs:163-175 ───
[maintainability · medium] `try_send` returning Err from a momentarily-full sync_channel(256)
permanently evicts the SSE client. A slow consumer (network blip, GC pause, slow downstream handler)
loses the connection and must reconnect through the replay path — and because dedup uses last_id,
the reconnect window can drop the very event that filled the channel. The `Weak<()>` liveness token
is also unused here (only consulted at registration per the comment), so writer threads that have
already exited but left their channel empty linger in the vec until the next failure. Distinguish
disconnect (upgrade Weak, return Err if dead) from backpressure (return Pending; let the writer
decide) and have a separate eviction path for confirmed-dead clients.

[maintainability · medium] Per-request workers are spawned via std::thread::spawn with the
JoinHandle immediately dropped, so they are detached from the lifecycle of `RunningApi`. Setting
shutdown.store(true) only breaks the accept loop — any handler already executing handle_request
keeps running and can still call emit_fn, mutate the TaskStore, or write to the audit log after
api_stop returns. This contradicts the documented "graceful stop" expectation and leaves callers
with no way to wait for in-flight requests to drain or to enforce a stop deadline. Track worker
JoinHandles (or a generation counter with a shared WaitGroup / atomic counter that drops to zero on
worker exit) and join them in api_stop with a bounded timeout, so callers know when shared state is
truly quiescent.

where the conservative `None` policy means a user selecting `High` will produce `reasoning=none` in
the audit log — indistinguishable from `Off`. The comment justifies this as anti-400 safety, but it
leaves no observable difference between `Off` and `High` for these models. Worth confirming the
conservative default is the intended production behavior and, if so, surfacing it to the UI so users
do not expect reasoning on these models.

restarts, breaking the determinism contract the file claims (see test

`DefaultHasher` with a stable, deterministic hasher (e.g. `crc32fast`, `seahash` with fixed key, or
a hand-rolled FNV-1a) so the same input always produces the same suffix.

─── src-tauri/src/bot/mcp/mount.rs:0-0 ───
[performance · medium] `find_mounted` rebuilds the entire mounted table (every schema, every
description, every JSON serialization) on every dispatch, and `execute_mcp_tool` additionally
reloads the full MCP server config from disk via `spawn_blocking(load_config)` on every call. This
is the hot path of the agent tool loop — once per model tool_call — and grows linearly with the
number of mounted tools × config file size. The `used.insert(func.clone())` inside the loop in
`build_mounted_tools` also clones the candidate name twice per iteration. Cache the mounted entries
(invalidated when manager reports a change) and cache the looked-up `McpServerConfig` (or pass it
via the mounted entry, populated when the mount table is built). At minimum, avoid the double
`func.clone()` inside the dedup loop.

[bug · medium] `from_utf8_lossy` silently corrupts malformed input despite the doc claim that lines
are valid UTF-8. The function comment explicitly states: "`b'\n'`（0x0A）不会出现在多字节 UTF-8 序列内，整行 decode
安全". Since each line is delimited by `\n` and `\n` is not a UTF-8 continuation byte, full lines MUST
be valid UTF-8 (or contain only ASCII). Using `from_utf8_lossy` here:
1. Hides real encoding bugs (e.g., a buggy proxy emitting Latin-1, or a misconfigured gateway
emitting GBK bytes)
2. Replaces invalid bytes with U+FFFD, which then ends up in tool `arguments` strings → "合法 JSON
但内容损坏会被真实执行" — exactly the failure mode the doc warns about elsewhere

an audit and substitutes an empty/known-invalid marker).

```rust
pub fn drain_sse_lines(buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    let mut last_end = 0;
    for i in 0..buf.len() {
        if buf[i] == b'\n' {
            let line = &buf[last_end..=i];
            match std::str::from_utf8(line) {
                Ok(s) => lines.push(s.to_owned()),
                Err(_) => lines.push(String::from_utf8_lossy(line).into_owned()), // 上游真坏，至少不静默
            }
            last_end = i + 1;
        }
    }
    if last_end > 0 {
        buf.drain(..last_end);
    }
    lines
}
```

`resp.bytes_stream()` drain or connection-close signal; relying entirely on reqwest's drop

there's no audit event for "stream died with partial tool call". Consider logging partial state on
timeout.

thread.

Two concerns:
1. Under concurrent requests (multiple chat sessions in parallel), this serializes all audit writes
behind a blocking call on one executor thread, starving other tasks
2. With the current per-round audit cadence, blocking time compounds (5-10 audits per round ×
blocking cost each)

Recommend either:

sync
- Or making `write_event` itself async (then the closure would need to be `FnMut(...) -> impl

synchronous) and likely the same issue.

```rust
audit: &'a (dyn Fn(crate::audit::AuditLevel, &'static str, Vec<(&'static str, String)>)
         -> std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = ()> + Send + Sync>>
         + Send + Sync),
```
This would let `write_event` do async I/O properly.

if `StopGuard`'s interior mutability is `RefCell`-based (or if a future revision adds one). Add `+
Sync` to the trait bound so this is caught at compile time, and likewise for

─── src-tauri/src/bot_skills/scheduler.rs:0-0 ───
[performance] Synchronous `DB_WRITE_LOCK` held for the entire upsert, swallowing failures silently.
`persist_outcome_quiet` acquires the process-wide synchronous `DB_WRITE_LOCK` (same one used by
long-running main-window transactions) and blocks the scheduler's async task for the duration of
`upsert_skill_outcome`. If the main window holds the lock for a long write, every skill outcome
(Done / AwaitUser / Failed / Terminated) will block here instead of yielding, and on failure the
result is dropped with no telemetry — the only persistence side-effect in the entire scheduler, so
outcomes go missing with no signal to the admin. At minimum log failures to stderr/audit with enough
context to detect silent loss, and consider a bounded retry or non-blocking enqueue rather than a
sync `lock()` in an async path.

mutex, triggering the silent-recovery fallback in the next caller. Acquire `DB_WRITE_LOCK` after
`open_db` returns, so the critical section covers only the SQL write itself.

+         return sessions.to_vec();
+     }
+     // Stride-based spread: pick evenly across the most-recent-first ordering
+     // so we exercise older sessions rather than only the freshest N.
+     let step = sessions.len() as f64 / n as f64;
+     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n);
+     let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::with_capacity(n);
+     for i in 0..n {
+         let idx = ((i as f64) * step) as usize;
+         if seen.insert(idx) {
+             out.push(sessions[idx].clone());
+         }
+     }
+     out
  }

which gives at-least-once idempotency instead of an unreliable dedup baseline.

─── src-tauri/src/evolution/candidate/entry.rs:81-84 ───
[bug · medium] Doc claim that POSIX O_APPEND makes a single `write()` to a regular file atomic is
too strong. POSIX only guarantees byte-atomicity for writes up to PIPE_BUF (typically 4096 bytes on
Linux); for serialized ProposalEntry larger than that, two concurrent writers can interleave bytes
inside the kernel and shred the jsonl line. Either document the bounded-size assumption explicitly
(and enforce it, e.g. by failing fast on oversized payloads) or add a per-line CRC + length-prefix
so partial writes are detectable.

concurrently. If the referenced "批次 spec" does not actually provide flock / `O_EXCL`

id"; today Merge/Distill are too aggressive — they treat any two same-count merges as the *same*

(or another reader that triggers the same backup path on a different thread) can win the gap between
the existence check and the copy. This can produce two competing backups racing on the same target,
or silently lose the intended `.corrupt` snapshot if a peer wrote/removed it in between. The
"best-effort 取证" comment only justifies the loose read-then-write window for normal corruption, not
the lack of atomic-rename semantics here. Suggest using `std::fs::rename` into a unique backup name
(or `fs::copy` then verify, or claim an exclusive lock on the source path) so two readers cannot
both attempt the snapshot step in parallel.

simply surface as an unhelpful `打开 ... 失败` error if the file is removed between check and open —
prefer `File::open(...).map_err(|e| match e.kind() { NotFound => return Ok(vec![]), ... })`.

─── src-tauri/src/memory/consolidate/tests.rs:33-38 ───
[documentation · low] The doc comment claims "内容哈希定维（同内容同向量）" (content hash defines the dimension,
same content → same vector), but the implementation is `v[text.len() % 512] = 1.0`. (1) The
dimension is hard-coded to 512, not "content-defined". (2) Distinct strings with the same byte
length collide — this is *byte-length keying*, not content keying. Collisions actually occur in this
suite: e.g. "合并" and "条目" both map to v[6] (both are 6 UTF-8 bytes), and "用户不吃辣（合并）" (27 B) collides
with the lesson content "偏好辛辣场景要谨慎" (27 B) in `apply_merge_excludes_evolution_lesson_rows`. If the
SUT ever consults these embeddings for similarity-based decisions during apply (e.g. to choose the
merge target or to short-circuit re-embedding), byte-length collisions can silently mask bugs. If
that risk is real, key on a content hash (e.g. `std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher`) or
simply include both length and a FNV-style mix of bytes so distinct strings with equal lengths
diverge.

the `waited >= 100 ms` assertion fails intermittently. Replace the bare `sleep` with a
`std::sync::Barrier` (start at 2, holder passes through it after acquiring the lock) or a oneshot
channel from holder → main to deterministically express the "holder owns the lock before main tries
to write" ordering intent without timing assumptions.

```rust
    }
```

}

before the loop and again inside each retry, doing redundant work; (2) the 99-iteration cap and the
"candidate" returned by the function are advisory — there is no actual claim (no temp file, no

concurrent migration that calls fs::create between exists() and the actual create can still trample

sentinel inside dst.parent to actually reserve the slot, or use an explicit lock around dst creation

```rust
pub(crate) fn claim_dst_name(dir: &Path, file_name: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let mut candidate = conflict_free_name(dir, file_name)?;
    for _ in 0..99 {
        if !candidate.exists() {
            return Some(candidate);
        }
        // 竞态窗口内被抢占：重选——conflict_free_name 跳过已存在名，必然递增后缀
        let next = conflict_free_name(dir, file_name)?;
        if next == candidate {
            return None; // 理论不可达（exists 时必换新名），防死循环兜底
        }
        candidate = next;
    }
    None
}
```

[other · medium] Cancellation safety: `migration_run`'s `spawn_blocking` task is detached on caller
drop. The blocking `run_migration` is moved into a `spawn_blocking` task and only observed via the
immediate `.await`; if the frontend cancels or closes mid-migration, the future is dropped, the
`JoinHandle` is dropped, and the destructive `move`/`delete` operations continue silently with no
observable result and no automatic cancellation (the `migration_cancel` command only fires if the
frontend explicitly invokes it). This is the exact "spawned tasks whose JoinHandle is dropped when
cancellation still needs to be observed" hazard the checklist calls out. Store a
`CancellationToken`/atomic flag, hand it to `run_migration`, and signal it via a drop-guard on the
command future. Also note that `CommandError::from(format!(...))` here discards the original
`JoinError`; use `CommandError::Internal(format!(...))` for clarity.

  pub async fn migration_run(app: AppHandle) -> CommandResult<MigrationReport> {
-     // B3: 主线程上不能跑长 IO（跨卷拷贝可冻结算分钟级）。
-     // 扔到 spawn_blocking 线程池，AppHandle 在子线程里仍可用（是 Send）。
-     tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || super::run::run_migration(&app))
-         .await
-         .map_err(|e| CommandError::from(format!("迁移线程 join 失败：{e}")))?
+     // 取消令牌：future 被 drop 时（前端关闭/取消请求）自动通知 run 线程停止，
+     // 避免 spawn_blocking 任务因 JoinHandle 被丢弃而"游离"继续做破坏性文件操作。
+     let cancel = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
+     let cancel_for_task = cancel.clone();
+     let app_for_task = app.clone();
+     let join = tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
+         super::run::run_migration(&app_for_task, cancel_for_task)
+     });
+     // Drop guard：future 在 .await 之前被 drop（例如前端关闭）时触发取消。
+     struct DropGuard(std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>);
+     impl Drop for DropGuard {
+         fn drop(&mut self) { let _ = self.0.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst); }
+     }
+     let _guard = DropGuard(cancel);
+     join.await
+         .map_err(|e| CommandError::Internal(format!("迁移线程 join 失败：{e}")))?

─── src-tauri/src/notifications.rs:49-60 ───
[bug · critical] Timestamps stored as TEXT but ordered by `created_at DESC` produces lexical
(byte-wise) sort in SQLite, not numeric sort. Millisecond Unix timestamps have varying digit counts
across years (10 digits before 2001, 13 digits after 2286), so "999…" (12-digit) > "1791…"
(13-digit) lexicographically even though 999e9 < 1791e9 numerically — the "新→旧" ordering guarantee
is silently wrong at the boundaries. Even when all rows are 13 digits, mixing in any
historical/legacy timestamps corrupts the list. Store as INTEGER (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY rowid is
already monotonic) and use `created_at INTEGER NOT NULL` (or drop the column and order by rowid
alone, since `INSERT OR IGNORE` preserves insertion order for new ids).

unparseable `resolved_at` is dropped entirely. Downstream the UI then renders a notification with
timestamp 1970-01-01 or no resolution date, with no signal back to the caller that the row is
broken. Either return a `rusqlite::Error::FromSqlConversionFailure` with the offending raw value, or
log+propagate with actionable context. Combined with the TEXT-timestamp storage this is the
proximate data-integrity hazard.



─── src-tauri/src/notifications.rs:214-227 ───
[performance · high] N+1 query pattern without transaction in `notif_sync_memory`: for each pending
memory notification, for each id in `payload.ids`, a separate `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mem_pending
WHERE id = ?1` is issued. With B notifications and avg I ids per payload this is O(B·I) round-trips.
More importantly there is no `BEGIN/COMMIT` wrapping the read-modify-write loop — if the process is
interrupted (or a single statement errors mid-loop) the table is left partially mutated, with some
notifications' payloads trimmed and others not. Fix with a single `SELECT id FROM mem_pending WHERE
id IN (rarray(?))` (use `rarray` from rusqlite or build a `?,?,?,?` placeholder list of bounded
size) plus a transaction around the loop.

─── src-tauri/src/ocr.rs:502-515 ───
[bug · high] Simplified DB post-processing uses 4-connectivity flood fill + rectangular unclip as a
coarse approximation of PaddleOCR's 8-connectivity flood fill + Vatti polygon expansion. This
directly degrades detection quality: 4-connectivity splits diagonally-touching text regions (a
single character or italic glyph becomes two boxes), and rectangular unclip over-expands tall/thin
boxes while under-expanding square ones. For a real document, expect visible missed/over-split
regions and degraded reading order. Consider 8-connectivity flood fill plus a Vatti-style polygon
expansion, or at minimum a 4-connectivity approach but with the unclip ratio applied asymmetrically
per side using box aspect ratio.

Furthermore, MIN_AREA = 10 pixels is very small and may keep noise; conversely there is no upper
bound on the seeded region size, so the heap-allocated `stack` Vec can grow to O(w*h) for a
fully-saturated map (10MB stack for a 1024×1024 input) — cap with a reservoir or switch to a
union-find labelling pass if large images are common.

Det model output is also assumed to be a single-channel probability map; `prob[..out_w*out_h]`
blindly takes the first H*W floats without verifying the channel count. A model revision emitting
[1, 2, H, W] (e.g., DB++ binary+threshold maps) would silently misinterpret the second channel as
probability.



─── src-tauri/src/ocr.rs:395-402 ───
[bug · high] Asymmetric and fragile ONNX shape handling. Det returns Err on rank mismatch (`if
shape.len() != 4 { return Err(...) }`), but rec silently `continue`s — a model revision that changes
output rank would silently drop every text block without any error or audit log entry. Even within
the rec branch, the silent skip (`if shape.len() != 3 { continue; }` and `if t == 0 || classes == 0
|| logits.len() < t * classes { continue; }`) hides data-integrity issues from both the caller and
the audit log. Unify the error handling: log a structured `ocr.rec_shape_skip` audit event when a
block is dropped, or surface a typed error to the user.

Related: `shape[2].max(0) as usize` on `Vec<i64>` produces a negative-to-usize underflow only if the
cast happens before the `.max(0)`; here `.max(0)` returns i64 and `as usize` will underflow if
shape[2] is negative. Models normally don't emit negative dims but the same expression is repeated
for `out_h`/`out_w` and `t`/`classes` — guard once at the boundary (`shape[i].max(0) as usize` only
after confirming non-negative, or saturate to 0 first).

─── src-tauri/src/ocr.rs:195-202 ───
[other · medium] `Mutex<ort::session::Session>` is held across the full `session.run()` call in
`run_first`, which is CPU-heavy ORT inference (and per-block in the rec/cls loops). All OCR calls
(one per `tool_ocr_image` invocation) are therefore strictly serialized on three separate locks,
even when the input images and model instances could in principle be processed in parallel. The
current design is documented as "串行足够", which is acceptable for a single-user CLI tool, but two
concerns remain:

1. `ort::session::Session`'s thread-safety contract is not visible in this file; the comment asserts
"Session 非线程安全语义由 Mutex 保证". If the underlying ONNX Runtime session is actually `!Send`/`!Sync`
(rather than merely "not safe to invoke concurrently"), the `Mutex<Session>` is fine; if Session has
internal thread-affinity (e.g., thread-local arena, GPU device context) the `Mutex<Session>` may
still be unsound even when locked, because the same Session may carry thread-local state established
at construction. Verify against the `ort` crate's documented `Send`/`Sync` impls and pinning
contract.

2. `Mutex::lock().map_err(|e| ...)` returns `Err(PoisonError)` and the function returns immediately,
leaking the lock holder. With three independent Mutexes (det/rec/cls) and sequential acquisition, a
panic in the middle of one inference does not poison subsequent lock acquisitions unless that same
thread panics again — so this is benign today, but the `eprintln!` audit is fire-and-forget; a
poisoned lock effectively disables OCR for the lifetime of the process. Consider reinitializing the
`ENGINE` OnceLock via `OnceLock::take`/`reset` on poison, or at minimum also log which Session
(det/rec/cls) was poisoned.

[bug · medium] Emoji prefixes (🤖/🔀/⏰/📦) function as string-typed enums that downstream logic uses to

drift, editor normalization, accidental replacement by similar-looking emojis). Because step 4
explicitly conditions the completion-marking rule on these prefixes, any change here silently flips
task-state semantics (e.g., a scheduled task gets marked complete → next tick won't fire). Either
parse these as a tagged enum at the boundary and map tothe canonical tool-call rules, or add a test
that asserts each prefix appears in exactly one branch of the policy.

running on different threads can emit events the listener receives in temporal order (i.e.
out-of-disk-order). Worth either (a) capturing the view inside the lock and emitting it after, or

easy to overlook when consumers rely on broadcast as the sole update path.

string length, otherwise the documented "free-form loop" fallback can be starved, infinite-looped,
or steered. Worth recording as a security-critical contract for the parser module, even though
enforcement lives elsewhere.

  pub fn dedup_dest(dir: &Path, name: &std::ffi::OsStr) -> std::path::PathBuf {
      let mut candidate = dir.join(name);
      let mut n = 1;
      while candidate.exists() {
          let p = std::path::Path::new(name);
          let stem = p.file_stem().unwrap_or(name).to_string_lossy();
          let new_name = match p.extension() {
              Some(ext) => format!("{stem} ({n}).{}", ext.to_string_lossy()),
              None => format!("{stem} ({n})"),
          };
          candidate = dir.join(new_name);
          n += 1;
      }
+     // Caller MUST retry on collision; the check here is best-effort.
      candidate
+ }
+

+     if copy_rec(&src, &dest).is_ok() && remove_rec(&src) {
+         ok = true;
+     } else {
+         let alt = dedup_dest(gen_dir, &name);
+         if copy_rec(&src, &alt).is_ok() && remove_rec(&src) {
+             ok = true;
+         }
+     }
  }

[bug · critical] **PID truncation produces a false positive that may issue `kill -9 --1`.**
`child.id()` is `u32`, but the cast to `i32` wraps for any pid > i32::MAX. For pid = 0xFFFF_FFFF the
cast yields `-1`, and POSIX `getpgid(-1)` is allowed to return `-1` (ESRCH on Linux) — so the
equality `-1 == -1` is true and `is_live_group_leader` reports a non-existent process as a group
leader. `kill_py_children` then builds the argument `--1` (i.e. PID -1), and the kernel's `kill(-1,
SIGKILL)` sends SIGKILL to every process the parent can signal — including unrelated processes on
the system. Gate the comparison on `pid <= i32::MAX as u32` (or use `as i64`) before doing the cast,
and return a distinct `ProbeError`/`Unavailable` instead of treating the negative case as
authoritative.

-     // SAFETY: pid 由调用方传入（subprocess 子进程 PID），本函数语义：若 getpgid(pid) == pid 则该 pid 是进程组 leader。
-     // POSIX getpgid(0) 返回调用方 PGID 是无害的（这里 pid 是入参，不会传 0）。返回值仅用于 == 比较，无 wrapper 误用风险。

+         return false; // u32 → i32 would wrap; refuse to classify.
+     }
+     let pid_i = pid as i32;
+     // SAFETY: pid_i is in [0, i32::MAX]; getpgid on a valid pid is async-signal-safe.
+     let pgid = unsafe { libc::getpgid(pid_i) };
+     pgid == pid_i
  }

[bug · medium] JSON escaping is incomplete in every SSE/Anthropic builder: only `\` and `"` are
escaped. If a test pushes content containing a literal `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, or any control char, it
will be embedded raw inside the `data: {json}` line — invalidating the JSON (raw newline inside a

malformed JSON, causing `parse_sse_chunk` / `parse_anthropic_event` to reject the event. Suggest a
small `escape_json_str(&str) -> String` helper that also escapes `\n` → `\\n`, `\r` → `\\r`, `\t` →
`\\t`, and other control chars per JSON spec, used uniformly by all builders.

─── clippy.toml:6-6 ───

This significantly loosens the lint: any function under 200 lines is now invisible to the linter

main loops') is reasonable, but the value should be chosen to still catch pathological cases.
Consider whether 200 is the right knob, or whether a more precise approach (e.g., keeping the
threshold lower and using `#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]` on the specific justified functions)
would preserve coverage without false positives.



─── clippy.toml:5-5 ───

deleted, or is not kept in sync with new code, the loose threshold will silently mask genuinely
oversized functions with no signal. Consider embedding the curated allow-list (e.g., per-function
`#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]` with a justification) inline in the source, so the policy is
self-documenting and version-controlled alongside the code it excuses.

via a `[build]` config that's only applied when `which sccache` succeeds, or by using a small shell
script that execs sccache or rustc directly).

test`, and CI runners. Combined with the (incorrect) fallback comment above, this means any
developer or CI environment that hasn't installed sccache will be unable to run cargo at all.
Consider scoping the wrapper conditionally (e.g., a wrapper shell script that execs sccache when
present and `rustc` otherwise) or document sccache as a hard prerequisite.

for `SCCACHE_DIR`, `SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE`, and a shared remote backend URL/key if a team-shared cache
is desired.

─── src/components/GraphPage/graph-adapter.ts:254-269 ───
[bug · high] Anchors for groups that are NOT a node's first-match group fall back to angle 0,
overlapping the first sector.

`groupOfNode` (lines 157-169) uses first-match-wins + `break` (line 165) and only contributes to
`groupKeys`/`sectorOf`. But `membersByGroup` (lines 240-250) is built from **all** tag→group
mappings of every node. So a group that some node reaches only as its 2nd/3rd tag will have members
≥ TAG_ANCHOR_MIN_CARDS, triggering anchor creation, but `sectorOf.get(group)` returns `undefined` →
anchor is placed at `Math.cos(0) * anchorR, Math.sin(0) * anchorR`. With multiple sector groups
present, all such "secondary" anchors stack on top of sector 0.

Fix: keep `groupOfNode` and `membersByGroup` consistent — either populate `groupOfNode` for **all**
matching groups (a node can belong to multiple sectors) or restrict `membersByGroup` to the same
first-match rule, so every group that gets an anchor also has a sector entry.



─── src/components/GraphPage/graph-adapter.ts:156-169 ───
[maintainability · medium] Placement (first-match-wins) and membership (all-matches) disagree on
which sector a multi-tagged node belongs to.

Line 164 uses `break` so a node is placed in only one sector, while line 243-249 adds the same node
as a member to **every** matching group. The node renders inside sector A but pulls toward anchor B
(and any other secondary anchors) at weight TAG_EDGE_WEIGHT=3. Beyond the visual overlap (see
anchor-fallback finding), this also biases FA2 in a way the sector/√N seed layout doesn't account
for.

Either align placement with membership (allow a node to live in multiple sectors — e.g. average over
its group sectors or pick one with a documented tiebreaker) or align membership with placement
(restrict `membersByGroup` to the same first-match rule). Pick one and apply consistently.



─── src/components/GraphPage/graph-adapter.ts:252-257 ───
[bug · medium] Anchor id can collide with a real task id; the existing check silently masks the
collision and the subsequent edge loop then wires tag edges to the real task.

`anchorId = "${TAG_ANCHOR_PREFIX}${group}"` (line 253) shares the same id namespace as task ids —
there is no convention/prefix-segregation enforced. If a real task happens to have id `taggrp:...`
(e.g. user-pasted id, schema-less import), `graph.hasNode(anchorId)` is true on line 256, the anchor
`addNode` is skipped, and the loop on lines 270-277 still adds edges `member → anchorId` with `kind:
"tag"`, weight 3. The real task silently becomes a "tag anchor": cluster layout breaks, degree
inflates, and downstream reducer logic that distinguishes `kind: "anchor"` from `kind: "task"` is
bypassed.

Fix: assert the namespace separation (e.g. `if (graph.hasNode(anchorId) &&
graph.getNodeAttribute(anchorId, "kind") !== "anchor") throw/return error`) or use a non-overlapping
id scheme (UUID for anchors, or check at the boundary where `built.nodes` is constructed).

[bug · high] setProfileName writes `cache` and notifies from `.then()` but never bumps `loadGen`. If
a `loadProfile(force=true)` is in flight and its response arrives after this set's response, the
in-flight force's `.then` will still pass `gen === loadGen` and overwrite `cache` with the older
snapshot — subscribers see stale data and any subsequent operation reading the cache sees the
pre-set value. The same race exists in `setProfileAvatar` (line 79) and `removeProfileAvatar` (line
88). Fix: bump `loadGen` (e.g., `++loadGen`) before the invoke so the in-flight force reload's
response is invalidated, matching the invariant described in the comment on line 20.



─── src/profile.ts:0-0 ───
[bug · medium] `listening` is flipped to `true` synchronously before the awaited `listen()`
resolves. If the `listen()` call rejects (Tauri IPC failure, missing capability, etc.), the
`.catch(() => {})` silently swallows the error and `listening` stays `true`, so every subsequent
`ensureProfileListen()` call early-returns and the `profile-changed` event is never wired up. The UI
then drifts out of sync with backend-driven profile changes with no log, no retry, and no surfaced
error. Fix: reset `listening = false` in the `.catch` (and optionally log/forward the error via
`handleCommandError`), so the next `loadProfile` retries registration.

across future loads. Either return a shallow copy (`return cache && { user: { ...cache.user }, bot:

[bug · high] splitAttachments regex is fragile and silently degrades to broken output. The pattern
is anchored at start-of-string with `^`, requires each list item to be terminated by `\n`, and
demands a trailing blank line (`\n` after the list). Any drift in format - CRLF line endings
(`\r\n`), a leading space before `[附件文件]`, no trailing blank line, or any future format tweak -
causes the whole match to fail and the raw `[附件文件]` header to be rendered inside the message body
(since `text` becomes the original content). For restored history messages this would look like a
broken bubble. Consider loosening the pattern (e.g., drop `^`, normalize CRLF, allow optional
trailing blank line) or at least strip the `[附件文件]` header even when the list isn't matched.

─── src/components/ChatPanel/ChatPanel.tsx:666-681 ───
[bug · medium] Tauri stream listener unmount race. Cleanup is `unlisten.then((f) => f())`, but the
listener registration Promise may resolve AFTER the cleanup runs. The race window between
`listen(...)` resolving (so the OS-level subscription is live) and the microtask that calls `f()` is
when a delta/think/tool/usage event can fire on an unmounted component. setMessages /
setSessionUsage / setConfirmReq will then be invoked on dead components (React 18 silently no-ops
with a dev warning; React 19 may warn harder and stale data can leak). Same risk in
`bot-skill-failed`, `bot-usage-delta`, etc. Suggest: track an `alive` flag set in the cleanup
function, guard each handler with `if (!alive) return;` before any setState, OR unsubscribe
synchronously if possible (Tauri 2 supports `unlisten()` returning a Promise but you can hold the
resolved unsubscribe in a ref synchronously via `then`).



─── src/components/ChatPanel/ChatPanel.tsx:0-0 ───
[bug · medium] Drag-drop listener leak on unmount. The cleanup is `return () => unlisten?.()`. If
the component unmounts before `onDragDropEvent(...).then((f) => unlisten = f)` resolves, `unlisten`
is still undefined and `unlisten?.()` is a no-op — the OS drag-drop subscription is registered on
the backend window but never torn down, and the captured `f` arrives later into a closure whose
target ref is gone. Additionally, the async `onDragDropEvent` callback can fire between unmount and
`.then` and call `setDragHover(...)` on an unmounted component. Suggest: use an `alive` flag (set
true in effect, false in cleanup) and guard all setState + the final `unlisten = f` assignment; or
move the unsub into a ref and call it from the `.then` if still alive.

[bug · high] The convergence "kinetic-energy" sampler is broken. `sum += |x - round(x)| + |y -
round(y)|` measures fractional distance to the nearest integer, not motion. A node moving by exactly
1 px per tick leaves `sum` unchanged → FA2 stops mid-flow (layout freezes before equilibrium).
Conversely, sub-pixel jitter around a non-integer position can vary `sum` while the layout has
effectively settled. Use actual displacement or velocity, e.g. `sum += |vx| + |vy|` (FA2 keeps
velocity attrs) or cache previous positions and compute `|x_t − x_{t−1}| + |y_t − y_{t−1}|`.

panning. Either remove it (Sigma already cancels pan during node-drag in normal cases) or replace
with a documented API like `sigma.getCamera().disableAnimation()?.()`. Also, the comment "阻止画布平移"

arriving in the same IPC batch, or any rapid sequence within one React batch), both callbacks see
the same `pendingRef.current` (typically null on the first event after mount, or the previously
committed value), so neither triggers the stale-reject invoke — only the last `setPending(p)` wins.

60s oneshot timeout (`bot_slash.rs:297-341`). Suggest: track the last accepted id in a
ref-or-variable that is updated synchronously *before* the `setPending` call (e.g.,
`pendingRef.current = p` immediately, then schedule a re-render), so the next event in the same task
can detect the previous one as stale and reject it. Add a regression test that emits two payloads in
the same `act()` block without awaiting render between them.

[bug · low] The stale auto-reject `invoke` is fire-and-forget and is not coordinated with the
`busyRef` re-entrancy guard. Although it does check `!busyRef.current` to skip when a response is

`respond` which sets busyRef and invokes for the *new* id. Both invokes are now in flight, the user
can keep clicking on the new modal (disabled by `busy`), and — more concerning — if the backend
processes the new-id response before the stale-id response, the backend's oneshot map for the old id
will time out anyway. This is mostly fine because the IDs differ, but the unbounded concurrent
invoke count is a latent risk. At minimum, route the stale reject through `respond` (e.g., a
`respond(false, { silent: true, allowWhenBusy: true })`) so it goes through the same

    let cur = 0;
    let i = active.length - 1;
    if (i >= 0 && !active[i]) i -= 1;
    for (; i >= 0 && active[i]; i -= 1) cur += 1;

      if (run > best) best = run;

─── .githooks/pre-push:3-3 ───
[bug · medium] Symlink / absolute-path fragility: `$(dirname "$0")/../scripts/test-all.sh` uses the
path git used to invoke the hook. If this hook is ever reached via a symlink (e.g.,
`.git/hooks/pre-push` is symlinked into `.githooks/pre-push`, or git invokes it via an absolute path
that points to a symlinked location), `$0` will be the symlink path and the script will resolve to
`<symlink-dir>/../scripts/test-all.sh` — i.e., the wrong directory — and silently skip the real test
gate (or run a stale/different copy). Resolve the real path first, e.g.:

```bash
HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || realpath "$0")")" && pwd)"
exec "$HOOK_DIR/../scripts/test-all.sh"
```

The repo currently uses `core.hooksPath = .githooks` so this is latent, but the hook is fragile to
any future relinking or `core.hooksPath` change.

- exec "$(dirname "$0")/../scripts/test-all.sh"
+ HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || realpath "$0")")" && pwd)"
+ exec "$HOOK_DIR/../scripts/test-all.sh"


─── .githooks/pre-push:3-3 ───
[maintainability · low] No pre-flight check for the target script. If `scripts/test-all.sh` is
missing (e.g., partial clone, wrong worktree, the file was renamed/moved) or lost its executable
bit, `exec` fails with bash's generic `No such file or directory` / `Permission denied` and the user
sees no hint that the repo's own test gate is broken — the push aborts with a confusing message
instead of a clear one. Add a defensive check so the failure mode is actionable:

```bash
TARGET="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || realpath "$0")")/../scripts/test-all.sh"
if [[ ! -x "$TARGET" ]]; then
    echo "pre-push: expected executable script at $TARGET (missing or not executable)" >&2
    echo "pre-push: refusing to push — fix scripts/test-all.sh or re-run scripts/install-hooks.sh"
>&2
    exit 1
fi
exec "$TARGET"
```

Let me structure the final output:

### Top Issues

1. **Silent mutex-poison recovery via `e.into_inner()` is the single most pervasive bug pattern**. A panicked thread holding a lock is followed by every later acquirer silently calling `e.into_inner()` and continuing on potentially half-mutated state. Hits at least 25 modules including `src-tauri/src/bot_skills/{runtime,scheduler,state,vars}.rs`, `src-tauri/src/db/{mod,bot_sessions,bot_history,schedule_jobs,subagents,workspace,trace,paths}.rs`, `src-tauri/src/api_handlers/{mod,commands,handlers,sse}.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/{activation,emit,sandbox/io,observe/shadow,observe/synthetic}.rs`, `src-tauri/src/memory/{consolidate,extract,panel,store}.rs`, `src-tauri/src/migration/{journal,recovery,ops}.rs`, `src-tauri/src/bot/{chat,orchestrator,slash,scheduler,fs,skills/manage,py/runtime,py/harvest}.rs`, `src-tauri/src/workflow_runner.rs`, `src-tauri/src/evolution/panel/commands.rs`. The cleanest single change is a `lock_db_write_or_recover()` helper that surfaces the prior panic to the caller instead of swallowing it.

2. **Typed error chains are flattened to `String` everywhere** (rusqlite, io, serde, reqwest, anyhow all → `.map_err(|e| e.to_string())`). 40+ sites in `src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs` alone; same pattern in `db/{tasks,workspace,people,schedule_jobs,bot_sessions,trace,bot_history,skill_out,workflow}.rs`, `memory/{store,extract,panel,consolidate,mod}.rs`, `evolution/{activation,emit,candidate/entry,candidate/mod,change/mod,change/status,change/derive,observe/{metrics,synthetic,stop,shadow},panel/commands,policy,sandbox/{io,kill_switch}}.rs`, `meta/{sync,mod}.rs`, `migration/{recovery,journal,ops,run,types}.rs`, `eval/{feedback,case,sampler,metrics,runner,config}.rs`. Every error-boundary `String` should be a typed `enum DbError { Rusqlite(rusqlite::Error), Io(io::Error), Serde(serde_json::Error), … }` so `command_error` can carry SQLSTATE / URL / variant info instead of a Chinese-localized format string.

3. **TOCTOU races on filesystem and jsonl state are widespread**. `src-tauri/src/bot_fs.rs` has multiple canonicalize-then-read/symlink/race windows (annotated as `[TOCTOU]`/`[DoS]`/`[fail-open]`), `bot_skills/manage.rs` (skills_import create_dir_all + copy), `bot_skills/files.rs` (recheck_canonical + opener/trash), `bot_chat.rs` (synchronous FS in async path), `evolution/candidate/mod.rs` (read_all + append dedup), `evolution/candidate/entry.rs` (jsonl append atomicity claimed but not enforced), `evolution/change/derive.rs` (unique_change_id_for), `evolution/sandbox/io.rs` (read_shadow/ab), `migration/{recovery,run,ops}.rs`, `db/tasks.rs` (delete_non_self_locked), `tag_similar.rs` (cache stampede). Almost none of them use `flock(2)` / `LOCK_EX` on the jsonl side.

4. **Tauri permission surface is wider than the threat model requires**. `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` grants `opener:allow-open-path $APPDATA/**` (covers local DBs, tokens, logs), `opener:default` is *also* listed so the scoped rule is undermined, identical permissions on `main` and `widget` windows, and `core:window:allow-current-monitor` exposes fingerprinting surface. `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` ships `'unsafe-eval'` in production CSP, enables `macosPrivateApi` unconditionally, ad-hoc signs macOS bundles with hardened Runtime disabled, and lists only "app"/"dmg" bundle targets while the icon set defines `.ico/.icns/.png` for NSIS. None of this is reversible from the frontend without a schema migration.

5. **Stringly-typed closed sets throughout**. Closed enums modeled as `String` lose compile-time checks in both directions: `src-tauri/src/migration/types.rs` (`op`, `action`), `src-tauri/src/mutation.rs` (protocol lowercase dup), `src-tauri/src/notifications.rs` (kind, status, payload keys), `src-tauri/src/bot/mcp/commands.rs` (state free-form String), `src-tauri/src/prompts/consolidate.rs` (LLM `action` allowlist), `src-tauri/src/db/bot_history.rs` / `error.rs` (`InvalidArgument.value`/`LlmApiError.body_preview` raw), `src-tauri/src/evolution/activation.rs` (`mode` free-form). Frontend mirror: `src/components/{SettingsPage,ChatPanel}/types.ts` declare "the only allowed values are X|Y|Z" in JSDoc but type the field as plain `string`, and `src/types.ts`'s `verdict: ... | string` collapses the literal union entirely. Fix is mechanical (typed enums + `TryFrom<String>`).

6. **`#[tauri::command]` `__cmd__` macro identifiers are re-flattened onto the production public surface**. `src-tauri/src/bot.rs` does `pub use {__cmd__bot_*, __tauri_command_name_bot_*}` to share with integration tests; `StopGuard`, `AuditLevel`, `PersistedSkillOutcome`, `load_all_skill_outcomes`, `upsert_skill_outcome` are `pub` *only* because `tests/llm_integration.rs` and `tests/skill_e2e.rs` construct them directly. The whole `tests/` integration suite also `Box::leak`s a `MockApp` per test (4+ leaks per session) because `MockRuntime` is not `Send`/`Sync`. This bleeds test scaffolding into the production crate boundary.

7. **Synchronous `std::fs` calls inside `async fn` block the Tokio worker**. Hits `bot_chat.rs` (attach_images_in, run_model_loop), `bot_model_loop.rs` (`audit` closure synchronous block), `bot_skills/state.rs` and `runtime.rs` (`audit_log_hook` while registry lock alive), `bot_skills/scheduler.rs` (DB_WRITE_LOCK + lock held across audit), `bot_tools.rs` (canonicalize + read on async path), `bot_fs.rs` (resolve_writable), `db/migrations.rs`, `db/bot_sessions.rs` (lock before `open_db`), `db/trace.rs`, `due_notify.rs` (notify_state mutex across I/O), `evolution/sandbox/io.rs` (SANDBOX_IO_LOCK across blocking I/O), `migration/rules.rs`, `migration/commands.rs`. Each of these can stall the runtime thread for tens-of-ms on every concurrent IPC.

8. **Shared mutable global state with no test isolation**: `src-tauri/tests/` files share `target/debug/deps/wmessage.db` and `bot-config.json`, `intent_router::ROUTES` is process-global and only restored on the happy-path panic, `SHARED_MCP_TEST_LOCK` (a `tokio::sync::Mutex`) poisons any test that panics mid-`lock().await`, `mock_handle()` `Box::leak`s a `MockRuntime` per call, the `cargo test` python tests run shared `BOT_LOG_LOCK` against the same file. Together these explain most of the "flake only on CI" comments.

9. **Hardcoded developer path / hardcoded business constants that drift**: `/Users/renshi/...` paths in `src-tauri/tests/audit_pre_step_pre_execute.py`, `examples/pbtest.rs`, `audit_pre_step_pre_execute.py`'s env PATH; `/tmp/no-such-bot-config-u20-xyz.json` in `evolution/policy.rs`; `bot-config.json` referenced as a bare filename in `eval/run.rs`; bot/params.rs hardcodes "100"/"8192"/"medium"/"60"/"不截断" defaults in two places that have no compile-time link. These are CI-environment-grade.

10. **Privacy / PII exposure in tests**: `src-tauri/tests/memory_eval.rs` writes real `model_inferred` memory text (profile/preference/fact) from the user's live SQLite to `fixtures/memory_extract_sample.jsonl`, with no atomic write — an interrupted run leaves a partial JSONL containing real user data on disk. `bot_web.rs`'s `fetch_text` silently exfiltrates URLs to `r.jina.ai` without opt-in when local extraction is short. `src-tauri/src/api_handlers/types.rs` keeps `ApiInfo.token`/`ApiStatus.token` as plaintext in every SSE payload, and `src-tauri/src/error.rs` ships raw `value`/`body_preview` fields over the wire.

- **Stringly-typed closed sets in both Rust and TypeScript** (TS comments name the closed set; field type is `string`). Sample: `migration/types.rs`, `mutation.rs`, `notifications.rs`, `bot/mcp/commands.rs` (`state`), `prompts/consolidate.rs` (`action`), `SettingsPage/types.ts` (`transport`, `state`), `ChatPanel/types.ts` (`PermMode` literal union), `types.ts` (`verdict`).
- **`Result<_, String>` everywhere**, fed by `.to_string()` on typed errors. Both faces flatten `rusqlite::Error`, `io::Error`, `serde_json::Error`, `reqwest::Error`, and `anyhow::Error` into opaque Chinese-localized format strings. Hits ~80 sites; see Top Issue #2.
- **Silent mutex-poison recovery** via `e.into_inner()` after bare `eprintln!`. See Top Issue #1 for the (non-exhaustive) list; every recovery site is a "panic-during-critical-section was lost" story.
- **Public-for-test surface leakage**: items declared `pub` solely so integration tests can name them (`bot.rs` StopGuard/AuditLevel/PersistedSkillOutcome/load_all_skill_outcomes/upsert_skill_outcome; the `__cmd__bot_*` macro ids), `tests/*` using `Box::leak(Box::new(tauri::test::mock_app()))` because `MockRuntime` is not `Send`/`Sync`.
- **TOCTOU / check-then-act**: `bot_fs.rs` (symlink, canonicalize-then-read), `migration/{journal,recovery,run,ops}.rs`, `evolution/candidate/mod.rs` and `entry.rs`, `tag_similar.rs`, `db/tasks.rs` (`delete_non_self_locked`), `evolution/sandbox/io.rs`, `bot_skills/{manage,files,state}.rs`.
- **`Vec::contains` / linear scans in hot paths** (should be `HashSet`): `bot_chat.rs` `merge_task_refs_dedup`, `evolution/derive.rs` `derive_mem_key`, `evolution/change/record.rs` `find_by_id/find_children/find_roots`, `evolution/change/derive.rs` `unique_change_id_for`, `memory/rank.rs` `pinned.iter().any`, `memory/consolidate.rs` `load_all` per op.
- **Tests with hardcoded TCP ports / hardcoded macOS paths / shared `wmessage.db`** without `#[serial]`/`flock`: `api_handlers/mod.rs` (`48821-48830`), `audit_pre_step_pre_execute.py` (`/Users/renshi/...`), `examples/pbtest.rs` (`/Users/renshi/...`), `tests/{skill_e2e,llm_integration,task_chat_exec,exec_trace,memory_v2_degraded,evolution_gov}.rs` all share the same `target/debug/deps/wmessage.db` + `bot-config.json` with documented-known pollute-and-cleanup races.
- **Synchronous FS / SQL inside `async fn`**: see Top Issue #7.
- **`let _ = h.join()` / `let _ = ...` / `.catch(() => {})`**: silently discards `JoinError` (which is the only carrier of panic payload+backtrace), `Result` from `audit::write_event`, `app.emit` failures, IPC teardown rejections. Hits `api_handlers/{commands,sse}.rs`, `lib.rs` (`api_stop_for_exit`/`wait_executions_drained`), `bot_slash.rs`, `bot_orchestrator.rs` (`spawn_subagent JoinHandle dropped`), `bot_skills/runtime.rs` (`spawn_blocking` JoinHandle dropped), `bot_skills/scheduler.rs`, `evolution/sandbox/io.rs` and `shadow.rs` (TOTAL_WRITES lifetime counter), `notifications.rs` (`ensure_table` per-call), `py/{io,document}.rs`, `App.tsx`/`ChatPanel.tsx`/etc. in the frontend.
- **Hardcoded constants that drift across three or more places**: `bot/params.rs` (PARAMS_TABLE defaults duplicated in `param_value` None branch), `evolution/derive.rs` (5-proposal cap with no impact bias), `error.rs` (code strings duplicated across enum variant + `#[serde(rename)]` + `as_str` match + `ALL` slice), `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (CSP/manifest), `vite.config.ts` / `vitest.config.ts` (assetsInlineLimit duplicated verbatim).
- **Both Tauri capability windows get the same allowlist** (`main` and `widget`) — over-broad surface for the mini widget.
- **`pub mod + pub use *` blanket re-exports** flatten encapsulation: `bot_skills/mod.rs`, `evolution/change/mod.rs`, `evolution/observe/mod.rs`, `src/components/SettingsPage/index.tsx`, `migration/mod.rs`.

### Quick Wins

- Replace every `e.into_inner()` mutex-recovery site with a single helper that surfaces the prior panic to the caller (`db::lock_or_panic()` returning `Result<MutexGuard, DbError>`). Touches ~40 sites in one mechanical pass.
- Replace every `let _ = std::fs::remove_file/write/rename` and `let _ = std::fs::set_permissions` with `Result<T, io::Error>` propagators in `api_auth.rs`, `audit.rs`, `bot_skills/state.rs`, `evolution/activation.rs`, `migration/{recovery,ops}.rs`. Restores audit trail without behavior change.
- Type the closed string sets: `enum ColumnId { Todo, Doing, Done }`, `enum MigrationAction { Move, Delete }`, `enum McpState { Connected, Down, Absent }`, `enum VerboseLevel { Concise, Detailed, Debug }`, `enum ReasonEffort { Off, Low, Medium, High }`, `enum PermMode { ReadOnly, Ask, Allow, Yolo }`. Frontend: `as const` literal tuples mirroring the Rust enum. Mechanical, but removes a large class of typo bugs across both languages.
- Replace `Vec::contains`/linear scans with `HashSet`/`HashMap` lookups in `bot_chat.rs::merge_task_refs_dedup`, `evolution/change/record.rs::find_by_id`, `evolution/change/derive.rs::unique_change_id_for`, `memory/rank.rs` (pinned iter), `memory/consolidate.rs::apply_ops_with` (`load_all` per op). Each is a one-line patch with measurable wins.
- Trim Tauri capability `default.json`: drop `opener:default`, scope `opener:allow-open-path` to the bot-config + keyring directories, remove the widget allowlist duplicates, drop `core:window:allow-current-monitor`/`allow-primary-monitor` unless used. In `tauri.conf.json`, drop `'unsafe-eval'` from production CSP, gate `macosPrivateApi` behind a dev profile, list `nsis` + `deb`/etc. alongside `app`/`dmg`.
- Strip the `unsafe-inline` devCSP host source / `--synthetic` silently overriding `--output` in `observe_run.rs`, the `--synthetic` flag should `eprintln!` and exit non-zero when both `--synthetic` and `--output` are set.
- Fix `bot-config.json` paths in `eval/config.rs` and `evolution/policy.rs` test fixtures (and the macOS `/Users/renshi/...` paths in `audit_pre_step_pre_execute.py`, `examples/pbtest.rs`) to derive from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` / `env!("OUT_DIR")` / `std::env::temp_dir()`.
- Tighten `.gitignore`: scope `README.txt` to `/README.txt`, un-ignore `.env.example` / `.env.template`, un-ignore `*.sln` (or scope to `/src-tauri/dotnet/**/*.sln`), drop the three `bot-api-key.txt` / `bot-tavily-key.txt` / `bot-brave-key.txt` concrete duplicates since `bot-*-key.txt` already covers them. Add `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `.idea/`, `.vscode/`, `*.swp`, `*~`.
- Add `// SAFETY:` rationale to every `unsafe` block in `py/runtime.rs::process_pid_truncation`, `bot_orchestrator.rs` (the few unsafe blocks it has), and `platform/copy_file.rs` (Windows CF_HDROP / macOS NSPasteboard) — the comments are missing or wrong in 6+ places.
- Replace `let _ = h.join()` with `match h.join() { Ok(()) => {}, Err(je) => audit!(level=error, "thread panicked: {je:?}") }` in `api_handlers/{commands,sse}.rs`, `bot_slash.rs`, `bot_skills/{runtime,scheduler}.rs`. Captures the panic payload before discarding.
- Tauri command arg key audit (compare Rust command `#[tauri::command]` arg structs vs. the camelCase keys the frontend sends): `error.rs`, `memory/{panel,extract}.rs`, `notifications.rs`, `types.ts`. Most misspellings are already latent; a single typed-deserialization table would expose them.
- Lock `test_handle` cleanup in `api_handlers/mod.rs` with a `#[serial]` mutex instead of hardcoding TCP ports `48821..48830`; same for `audit_pre_step_pre_execute.py::test_bot_log_path_uses_portable_dir` and the shared `wmessage.db` reads in `tests/{skill_e2e,llm_integration,exec_trace,task_chat_exec,memory_v2_degraded,evolution_gov}.rs`.
- Move the production panic-prone `unwrap_or_default()` (e.g. `bot_orchestrator.rs` gen_dir fallback `"__gen_dir__"`, `memory/store.rs::ts_to_ms`) to `Result<_, _>` early-returns so the caller decides the policy.
- Add `tracing::info!`/`warn!` next to the silent `eprintln!` sites in `audit.rs`, `evolution/{activation,observe/synthetic,observe/stop}.rs`, `py/audit.rs`, `migration/{recovery,journal,ops}.rs` — at minimum makes these visible in Tauri release builds where stderr is detached.
